input: scheduled: continue work on the repo (revenue products); routed to redteam

doc_friction.issue: Two concurrent redteam runs picked the same newly landed target (both following the 'aim at a file that just changed on main' advice) and duplicated the Infinity finding. A quick search of open redteam PRs for the target before the campaign would have avoided it.

notes: Step 0: all 13 open entries are control-plane (.github/workflows, prompts/) or the deferred help-keeper stemmer redesign; none fixable in a non-control-plane PR this run, left open. Target: window-design-pressure-calculator/calc.mjs (landed 2026-11-22, safety-relevant). 24 mutants, catch 0.864 -> 1.0. 2 real defects patched (header after # line; Number() accepting Infinity/hex), plus the same decimal-only parser fix in 7 sibling ventures (all suites green). Class guard not added: 29 other `t === "" ? NaN : Number(t)` copies exist; most check Number.isFinite afterwards so only hex slips through, which is low severity. A lint is a candidate for a later run. Local verification: run_workflow_locally --for-changes passed 7/7 selected workflows. The uses: steps and the cross-review/deploy jobs did not run locally; portfolio-pages and portfolio-validate were deferred to PR CI. check_posts ok, promptctl validate ok, redteam rerun: all 3 gaps caught_after_fix true. Merge conflict with the parallel red-team PR #18479 on the same target, resolved by combining both fixes.

real_defects.issue: parseOpenings skipped a header only on raw line 1, though the page promises 'A header row and lines starting with # are skipped' and the sample opens with a # line: keeping it (or a leading blank line) and pasting 'Mark, Width, Height' returned an error; 'Opening, W, H' headers never matched the width|label|mark regex. Fixed: the first content line with text width and height is the header.

num() used Number(), so 'Infinity' and hex ('0x8C') were accepted from text inputs and shared links: leastDim=Infinity gave corner zone width a = Infinity ft (every opening zone 5, 'Infinity ft' on the page), V=0x8C ran as 140 mph. Fixed: plain decimals only. The Infinity half was found and fixed in parallel by PR #18479, which merged first. This run merged the two fixes (decimal regex plus isFinite) and kept both test sets.
